newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris bourse closes higher on new government.
newsitem.headline: Paris bourse closes higher on new government.

text.p: French shares close more than two percent higher, bolstered by relief at the composition of France's Socialist-led government. It includes a known quantity as finance minister, Dominique Strauss-Kahn, and assigns only one big portfolio, transport, to the Communists.
* CAC-40 index closes up 55.48, or 2.11 percent, at 2,690.85
* CAC-40 June futures 2,685 vs 2,684 at Thursday's close
* Volume 11.9 billion francs, among the heaviest for year

French stocks rose sharply on Thursday, but ended off their session highs when the blue-chip CAC-40 was up more than three percent, on investor relief with the composition of the new Socialist-led government.
Brokers said the rise was also fuelled by short-covering and technical factors, and several said the market was due for a pause.

"The rise was a bit exaggerated. I think we'll see a bit of consolidation tomorrow," one trader said. The market is also expected to slow down a bit on Friday after five days of gains ahead of the U.S. employment report for May due at 1230 GMT.

"We've suddenly discovered the virtues of the Socialists which the market considered lower than the ground before the runoff vote -- the scenario of a weak euro ... due to deficits is seen as favourable for the bourse and dollar," said Hugues de Montvallon, economist at Oddo.

Rumours of a delay in the timetable for European Monetary Union -- denied by the government -- weighed on the market in the afternoon and signalled its sensitivity to the new government's pronouncements. "The market will now be waiting for indications on specific policies," a trader said.

* Rally adds to gains of this week's stars, consumption, retail and building company shares seen beneficiaries from a government on the left. Retail Promodes closes up 4.96 percent at 2,115 francs and building materials group Lafarge up 5.28 percent at 385 francs.

* Hotel group Accor rose 5.72 percent on the chairman's bullish results forecasts at Wednesday's annual general meeting and a report in the newspaper La Tribune that investor George Soros holds 2.18 percent.
* Sanofi rose 5.81 percent to 546 francs on three new compounds expected to boost sales.
* Societe Generale SOCG.PA gained 3.05 percent, recovering part of its recent losses on concerns about the bank sector's restructuring pace under the new government.

* Suez and Lyonnaise are the only losers on the CAC, falling 0.55 percent and 0.72 percent on disappointment with the proposed merger of Belgium's Electrabel and its parent company Tractebel that would dilute their stake in Tractebel.
